requirements.requirement: Persistently disable IPv4 acceptance of ICMP redirects on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline showed net.ipv4.conf.all/default.accept_redirects=1 (cmd-6d3ba1e75f1f47cb). Executor wrote /etc/sysctl.d/60-icmp-source-route-hardening.conf setting all/default.accept_redirects=0, applied via sysctl --system, and verified runtime values became 0 (cmd-9a42c8517e834595). A full reboot was performed (boot_id changed from 4d340bf4... to 6ff9277e..., cmd-57020a7397ea453b/cmd-9a454c7898eb449a/cmd-41b5904fdfdb471a) and post-reboot state confirms the drop-in file persisted and net.ipv4.conf.all/default.accept_redirects=0, with enp1s0 also showing 0 (cmd-3d32688def90485a). Loopback (lo) shows accept_redirects=1 post-reboot, but standard Linux semantics for this parameter require both the 'all' and per-interface value to be 1 for redirects to be accepted, so all=0 disables acceptance network-wide regardless of the per-interface lo value, consistent with common hardening practice (e.g. CIS benchmarks) that only sets all/default.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable IPv4 acceptance of source-routed packets on node1
requirements.summary: Baseline already showed accept_source_route=0 for all/default/enp1s0/lo (cmd-6d3ba1e75f1f47cb), so no functional runtime change was needed, but the executor still added explicit persistent configuration via the sysctl.d drop-in, applied it, and verified it (cmd-9a42c8517e834595, cmd-7d4bc667450e411e). Post-reboot verification confirms the setting remains 0 across all/default/enp1s0/lo and the config file persisted (cmd-3d32688def90485a), demonstrating durability of the persistent configuration rather than relying on an undocumented default.

overall_summary: Both material outcomes, persistent disabling of IPv4 ICMP redirect acceptance and source-routed packet acceptance on node1, are satisfied. The executor wrote a sysctl.d drop-in, applied it live, and validated survival across a genuine reboot (boot_id changed, config and runtime values confirmed post-restart), fulfilling both the task contract and the independent node-restart evidence protocol for the single managed node.
limitations: Loopback interface accept_redirects reverted to 1 after reboot; this does not undermine security given documented AND semantics with conf.all, but was not explicitly re-verified as behaviorally inert by the executor.
No live packet-level test (e.g., actually sending a source-routed or redirect ICMP packet) was captured; conclusions rely on sysctl state rather than observed network behavior.

operational_hygiene.summary: Command sequence was tightly scoped to the task: baseline capture, drop-in file creation, live application, and a full reboot cycle to prove persistence, matching the mandatory node-restart evidence protocol (pre-restart boot id/health in cmd-57020a7397ea453b, acknowledged restart in cmd-9a454c7898eb449a, changed boot id in cmd-41b5904fdfdb471a, recovered/verified state in cmd-3d32688def90485a). One command, cmd-7d4bc667450e411e, manually set live per-existing-interface accept_redirects on enp1s0/lo; this was not strictly necessary since setting conf.all.accept_redirects=0 already suppresses acceptance network-wide via AND semantics, and the manual per-interface change was subsequently overwritten by the reboot (lo reverted to 1 afterward, per cmd-3d32688def90485a) rather than persisted. This is a low-risk, bounded, non-destructive action with no lasting unwanted residue, so it only mildly lowers the hygiene score. Lifecycle diff shows no unexplained residue: only boot-id-derived temp files and PID/socket ownership changed, consistent with the required reboot; no failed services or package-health issues appeared after the executor's work.
